quotes.text: On the field of justice, the Kuru-field, my men and the sons of Pāndu too [stand] massed together ready for the fight. What, Sanjaya, did they do?
quotes.cite: Dhritarashtra; Chapter 1, verse 1; Robert Charles Zaehner translation

quotes.text: Now seeing the armies of the Pandavas arrayed in battle formation,King Duryodhana, approaching his teacher, spoke these words: Behold these mighty warriors of the sons of Pandu, O Revered Teacher, Arrayed in battle formation by the son of Drupada, your own skillful student.
[Duryodhana said:] This force of ours guarded by Bhishma is unbounded; although this force, of theirs – guarded by Bhima, is bounded.
quotes.cite: Sanjaya; Chapter 1; verse 10; Laurie L. Patton translation

quotes.text: Hrishikesha blew the conch shell named Panchajanya and Dhananjaya blew the conch shell named Devadatta. Vrikodara, whose deeds give rise to fear, blew the giant conch shell named Poundra.
quotes.cite: Sanjaya; Chapter 1, verse 15; Bibek Debroy translation

quotes.text: The blowing of these different conchshells became uproarious, and thus, vibrating both in the sky and on the earth, it shattered the hearts of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
quotes.cite: Verse 19, Swami Prabhupada translation, 1972

quotes.text: All those for whom i'd want to live it up are here to die
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 1, verse 33; Mani Rao translation

quotes.text: And even if, because their minds are overwhelmed by greed, they cannot see the evil incurred by destroying one's own family, and the degradation involved in the betrayal of a friend, How can we be so ignorant as not to recoil from this wrong? The evil incurred by destroying one's own family is plain to see, Janardana.
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 1, verses 38–39; W. J. Johnson translation

quotes.text: Out of the corruption of women proceeds the confusion of castes; out of the confusion of castes, the loss of memory; out of the loss of memory, the lack of understanding; and out of this, all evils
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 1, verses 41-44; based on Emile Burnouf’s translation

quotes.text: What is this crime I am planning, O Krishna? Murder most hateful,Murder of brothers!Am I indeed So greedy for greatness?
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 1, verse 45; Swami Prabhavananda and Christopher Isherwood translation

quotes.text: If me unresisting, Weaponless, with weapons in their hands Dhritarāshtra's men should slay in battle,That would be a safer course for me.
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 1, verse 46; Franklin Edgerton translation

quotes.text: Thus speaking Arjuna in the battle Sat down in the box of the car, Letting fall his bow and arrows, His heart smitten with grief.
quotes.cite: Sanjaya; Chapter 1, verse 47 (the last verse in the chapter); Franklin Edgerton translation

quotes.text: My dear Arjuna, how have these impurities come upon you? They are not at all befitting a man who knows the progressive values of life. They do not lead to higher planets, but to infamy. O son of Prtha, do not yield to this degrading impotence. It does not become you. Give up such petty weakness of heart and arise, O chastiser of the enemy.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verses 2–3; A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada translation

quotes.text: My Lord! How can I, when the battle rages, send an arrow through Bheeshma and Drona, who should receive my reverence?
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 2, verse 4; Shri Purohit Swami translation

quotes.text: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for; yet you speak wise words.Neither for the dead nor those not dead do the wise grieve.Never was there a time when I did not exist nor you nor these lords of men. Neither will there be a time when we shall not exist; we all exist from now on. As the soul experiences in this body childhood, youth, and old age, so also it acquires another body; the sage in this is not deluded.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verses 11–13; Sanderson Beck translation

quotes.text: The senses, moving toward their appropriate objects, are producers of heat and cold, pleasure and pain, which come and go and are brief and changeable; these do thou endure, O son of Bharata!
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verse 14; Charles Wilkins

quotes.text: As you put on fresh new clothes and take off those you've worn, You'll replace your body with a fresh one, newly born.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verse 22; Carl E. Woodham

quotes.text: Swords cut him not, nor may fire burn him, O son of Bharata, waters wet him not, nor dry winds parch. He may not be cut nor burned nor wet nor withered; he is eternal, all-present, firm, unshaken, everlasting. He is called unmanifest, unimaginable, unchanging; therefore, knowing him thus, deign not to grieve!
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verses 23–25; Charles Johnston

quotes.text: One sees This as a wonder; another speaks of This as a wonder; another hears of This as a wonder; yet, having heard none understands This at all!
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verse 29; Swami Chinmayananda commentary

quotes.text: Either slain thou shalt go to heaven; or victorious thou shalt enjoy the earth. Therefore arise, O Son of Kuntī (Arjuna), resolved on battle.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verse 37; Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan translation

quotes.text: You are only entitled to the action, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruits of action be your motive, but do not attach yourself to nonaction.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verse 47; Lars Martin Fosse translation

quotes.text: The wise, engaged in devotional service, take refuge in the Lord, and free themselves from the cycle of birth and death by renouncing the fruits of action in the material world. In this way they can attain that state beyond all miseries.
quotes.cite: Krsna, Text 51, Swami Prabhupada translation, ISKCON, 1972

quotes.text: When your intelligence has passed out of the dense forest of delusion, you shall become indifferent to all that has been heard and all that is to be heard.
quotes.cite: Krsna, Text 52, Swami Prabhupada translation, ISKCON, 1972

quotes.text: When your mind is no longer disturbed by the flowery language of the Vedas, and when it remains fixed in the trance of self-realization, then you will have attained the Divine consciousness.
quotes.cite: Krsna, Text 53, Swami Prabhupada translation, ISKCON, 1972

quotes.text: When your intellect transcends the mire of delusion, then you will attain to disgust of what has been heard and what is yet to be heard. When, perplexed by what you have heard, you stand immovable in samadhi, with steady intellect, then you will attain yoga.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verses 52–53; Jeaneane D. Fowler translation

quotes.text: When one's mind dwells on the objects of Senses, fondness for them grows on him, from fondness comes desire, from desire anger. Anger leads to bewilderment, bewilderment to loss of memory of true Self, and by that intelligence is destroyed, and with the destruction of intelligence he perishes
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verses 62–63

quotes.text: To him [the Sage], what seemeth the bright things of day to the mass, are known to be the things of darkness and ignorance—and what seemeth dark as night to the many, he seeth suffused with the light of noonday.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 2, verse 69; Yogi Ramacharaka edition

quotes.text: If thou deemest that (the path of) understanding is more excellent than (the path of) action, O Janardana (Krishna), why then dost thou urge me to do this savage deed, O Kesava (Krishna)?
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 3, verse 1; Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan translation

quotes.text: Not by not acting in this world does one become free from action, nor does one approach perfection by renunciation only. Not even for a moment does someone exist without acting. Even against one’s will, one acts by the nature-born qualities.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 3, verses 4–5; Gavin Flood and Charles Martin translation

quotes.text: From food come forth beings; from rain food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain, and sacrifice is born of action. Know you that action comes from BRAHMAJI (the Creator) and BRAHMAJI come from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading BRAHMAN (God-principle) ever rests in sacrifice.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 3, verses 14–15; Swami Chinmayananda commentary

quotes.text: Not for me, partha, is there any duty in the three worlds, nor anything to attain that is unattained; and I am always at work.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 3, verse 22; Ramesh Menon translation

quotes.text: All actions are performed by the gunas of prakriti. Deluded by identification with the ego, a person thinks, "I am the doer.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 3, verse 27; Eknath Easwaran translation

quotes.text: One's own duty, even if imperfectly performed, is better than being done by other even if well performed. Death in (performance of) one's own duty is preferable. (The adoption of) the duty of another carries fear (with it).
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 3, verse 35; Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation

quotes.text: I explained this eternal science of yoga to Vivasvān. Vivasvān shared it with Manu, then Manu imparted it to Ikṣvāku. This science was taught and handed down in succession, but in time it was broken and the science of yoga seems to be lost.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verses 1–2; The Times of India

quotes.text: Although I am unborn and My transcendental body never deteriorates, and although I am the Lord of all sentient beings, I still appear in every millennium in My original transcendental form. Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion — at that time I descend Myself. In order to deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of religion, I advent Myself millennium after millennium.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Verses 6, 7, & 8. Swami Prabhupada translation (1972)

quotes.text: Whensoever there is the fading of the Dharma and the uprising of unrighteousness, then I loose myself forth into birth. For the deliverance of the good, for the destruction of the evil-doers, for the enthroning of the Right, I am born from age to age.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verses 7–8; Sri Aurobindo translation

quotes.text: However men try to reach me, I return their love with my love; whatever path they may travel, it leads to me in the end.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verse 11; Stephen Mitchell translation

quotes.text: The four divisions of human order were created by me according to differences in quality, activities, and aptitude; although the creator of this, know me as the non-doer being immutable.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verse 13; Bhagavad-Gita Trust translation (1998)

quotes.text: Depending upon the distribution of the three attributes or guṇas and actions, I have created the four castes. Yet, I am to be known as the non-doer, the unchangeable.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verse 13; as translated by Paramahamsa Nithyananda (2011) translation

quotes.text: Works do not stain me, nor in me is there longing for fruit of works; who recognizes this to be my state, he is not bound by works.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verse 14; W. Douglas P. Hill translation

quotes.text: For verily (the true nature) of 'right action' should be known; also (that) of 'forbidden (or unlawful) action' and of 'inaction'; imponderable is the nature (path) of action. He who recognises inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among men; he is a YOGI and a true performer of all actions.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verses 17–18; Swami Chinmayananda commentary

quotes.text: Kill therefore with the sword of wisdom the doubt born of ignorance that lies in thy heart. Be one in self-harmony, in Yoga, and arise, great warrior, arise.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 4, verse 42 (the last verse in the chapter); Juan Mascaró translation

quotes.text: You commend, O Krishna, the renunciation of action and you also praise yoga. Tell me definitely which is the better of the two.
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 5, verse 1; B. Srinivasa Murthy translation

quotes.text: Both renunciation and the yoga of action lead to the supreme good. But of these two, performance of action is superior to the renunciation of action.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 5, verse 2; B. Srinivasa Murthy translation

quotes.text: He is unaffected by Karma, although engaged in action, who has yoked himself to the way of Yoga, whose mind is purified, whose self has triumphed and whose senses have been subdued, and whose self has, indeed, become the self of all beings. Although acting he remains unaffected by Karma.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 5, verse 7; C. Rajagopalachari translation

quotes.text: The humble sages, by virtue of true knowledge, see with equal vision a learned and gentle brahmana, a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dog-eater [outcaste].
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 5, verse 18; translation source with commentary

quotes.text: As enjoyments, born of contacts (with external objects), have a beginning and an end, they become the cause of unhappiness. The wise man, O Kaunteya! does not find happiness in them.
To the sage who wishes to rise to devotion, action is said to be a means, and to him, when he has risen to devotion, tranquillity is said to be a means.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 6, verse 3; Kashinath Trimbak Telang translation

quotes.text: Use the atman to raise the atman. Do not lower the atman. The atman is the atman’s friend and the atman is the atman’s enemy. The atman, which has been used to conquer the atman, is the atman’s friend. For someone who has failed to control the atman, the atman harms like an enemy.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 6, verses 5–6; Bibek Debroy translation

quotes.text: Who sees Me everywhere, and sees all in Me, him I lose not, nor will he lose Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 6, verse 30; Charles Johnston translation

quotes.text: O Madhusūdana, the mind is an unsteady thing. Hence it is unrealistic to expect evenness out of it as your system of yoga demands. O, Keśava, it is easier to control the wind than to try and control the fickle, unsettling, dominant, and stubborn mind.
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 6, verses 33–34; The Times of India translation

quotes.text: O strong armed arjuna no doubt the mind's moves are hard to stay you get a grip by practice & undifference
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 6, verse 35; Mani Rao translation

quotes.text: The yogin is greater than the ascetic; he is considered to be greater than the man of knowledge, greater than the man of ritual works, therefore do thou become a yogin, O Arjuna.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 6, verse 46; Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan translation

quotes.text: Among thousands of men hardly one strives after perfections; among those who strive hardly one knows Me in truth.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 7, verse 3; Mahatma Gandhi translation

quotes.text: This divine illusion of Mine, caused by the qualities, is hard to pierce; they who come to Me, they cross over this illusion.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 7, verse 14; Annie Besant translation

quotes.text: I am not plain to all, being cloaked by my yogamaya; this foolish world does not know me: un-born, immortal.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 7, verse 25; Ramesh Menon translation

quotes.text: I know all past and all present and future existences, O Arjuna, but Me none yet knows.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 7, verse 26; "Bhagavad Gita and Its Message", by Sri Aurobindo, edited by Anilbaran Roy

quotes.text: Yogis not yet free from the world revolve back again (to the world) even from the high sphere of Brahma (union with God in samadhi). But on entering into Me (the transcendental Spirit) there is no rebirth, O son of Kunti (Arjuna)!
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 8, verse 16; Paramahansa Yogananda translation

quotes.text: As an eon ends, all creatures fold into my nature, Arjuna; and I create them again as a new eon begins. Gathering in my own nature, again and again I freely create this whole throng of creatures, helpless in the force of my nature.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 9, verses 7–8; Barbara Stoler Miller translation

quotes.text: But those acts do not affect Me, Arjuna – >I am neutral, unattached.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 9, verse 9; Purushottama Lal translation

quotes.text: For Nature while I supervise gives birth to moving and unmoving, and as this motive-force applies the cosmos is revolving.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 9, verse 10; Geoffrey Parrinder translation

quotes.text: Fools scorn me when I dwell in human form: my higher being they know not as Great Lord of beings.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 9, verse 11; W. Douglas P. Hill translation

quotes.text: Even those who are devotees of other gods and sacrifice to them with faith, they too worship me — but in the wrong way
quotes.cite: Krishana: Chapter 9, verse 15 Doniger, Wendy. On Hinduism (p. 15). Oxford University Press.

quotes.text: I take upon Myself the concern for the welfare of those who worship Me with undistracted mind, and have thereby yoked themselves permanently to Divine Spirit.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 9, verse 22; C. Rajagopalachari translation

quotes.text: For even if the greatest sinner worships me with all his soul, he must be considered righteous, because of his righteous will. And he shall soon become pure and reach everlasting peace. For this is my word of promise, that he who loves me shall not perish.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 9, verses 30–31; Juan Mascaró translation

quotes.text: Worlds of flesh and spirit both originate with Me. Sages understand this well and serve me earnestly. My devotees think of Me and serve Me all the time. Speaking of Me makes their lives delightful and sublime.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 10, verses 8–9; Carl E. Woodham translation

quotes.text: Of the Vrishnis, I am Vasudeva; of the sons of Pandu, Arjuna; of the sages, moreover, I am Vyasa; of poets, the poet Ushana.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 10, verse 37; Winthrop Sargeant translation

quotes.text: Arjuna said: My illusion is dispelled by Your profound words, that You spoke out of compassion towards me, about the supreme secret of the Self. O Krishna, I have heard from You in detail about the origin and dissolution of beings, and Your imperishable glory. O Lord, You are as You have said, yet I wish to see Your divine cosmic form, O Supreme Being. O Lord, if You think it is possible for me to see this, then O Lord of the yogis, show me Your imperishable Self. V. 1, 2, 3 & 4

The Supreme Lord said: O Arjuna, behold My hundreds and thousands of multifarious divine forms of different colors and shapes. See the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ashvins, and the Maruts. Behold, O Arjuna, many wonders never seen before. O Arjuna, now behold the entire creation; animate, inanimate, and whatever else you like to see; all at one place in My body. But, you are not able to see Me with your physical eye; therefore, I give you the divine eye to see My majestic power and glory. V. 5-8
Tell me who are You in such a fierce form? My salutations to You, O best of gods, be merciful! I wish to understand You, the primal Being, because I do not know Your mission. V.31

The Supreme Lord said: I am death, the mighty destroyer of the world, out to destroy. Even without your participation all the warriors standing arrayed in the opposing armies shall cease to exist. The Lord said: I am Time, the mighty force which destroys everything, fully Manifesting Myself, I am here engaged in destroying the worlds. Even without you, none of the warriors arrayed in the enemy ranks shall survive.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 11, verse 32; Paramahamsa Vishwananda translation

quotes.text: Saying thus to Arjuna, Krishna revealed again his own familiar form. Having thus assumed that gentle form, the Exalted One comforted the awe-struck Arjuna over again.
quotes.cite: Sanjaya; Chapter 11, verse 50; Swami Tapasyananda translation

quotes.text: This My form, which you have seen, is very difficult to see. Even the gods always desire to see this form. It is not possible for any one to see Me, as you have seen Me, whether by Vedas, or by austerity, or by charity, or by Yajnās. O Arjuna! only by exclusive devotion, is it possible to thus acquire knowledge of Me, and O Parantapa! to enter Me essentially.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 11, verses 52–54; Bal Gangadhar Tilak translation

quotes.text: Which is considered to be more perfect, those who are properly engaged in Your devotional service, or those who worship the impersonal Brahman, the unmanifested?
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 12, verse 1; A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada translation

quotes.text: The Blessed Lord said: Those who, fixing their minds on Me, adore Me, ever united to Me with supreme devotion, are in My eyes the perfect knowers of yoga.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 2; Paramahamsa Yogananda's translation

quotes.text: But those who seek after the indefinable unmanifested, immutable, omnipresent, unthinkable, self-poised, immobile, constant, having subdued all their senses, unprejudiced, intent on the welfare of all beings - they too come to Me alone.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verses 3-4; Paramahamsa Vishwananda's translation

quotes.text: The difficulty of those who devote themselves to the search of the unmanifested Brahman is greater; it is a think to which embodied souls can only arrive by a constant mortification, a suffering of all the repressed members, a stern difficulty and anguish of the nature.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 5; Paramahamsa Vishwananda's translation

quotes.text: But those who giving up all their actions to Me, and wholly devoted to Me, worship meditating on me with an unswerving Yoga, those who fix on Me all their consciousness, O Paartha, speedily I deliver them out of the sea of death-bound existence.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verses 6-7; Paramahamsa Vishwananda's translation

quotes.text: On Me repose all your mind and lodge all thy understanding in Me; doubt not that you shall dwell in Me above this mortal existence.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 8; Paramahamsa Vishwananda's translation

quotes.text: And if you are not able to consciousness fixed steadily in Me, then by the Yoga of practice seek after Me, O Arjuna.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 9; Paramahamsa Vishwananda's translation

quotes.text: If you are unable even to seek by practice, then be it your supreme aim to do My work; doing all actions for My sake, you shall attain perfection.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 10; Paramahamsa Vishwananda's translation

quotes.text: But if even this constant remembering of Me and lifting up of your works to Me is felt beyond your power, then renounce all fruit of action with the self-controlled.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 11; Paramahamsa Vishwananda's translation

quotes.text: Verily, wisdom (born from yoga practice) is superior to (mechanical) yoga practice; meditation is more desirable than the possession of (theoretical) wisdom; the relinquishment of the fruits of action is better than (the initial states of) meditation. Renunciation of the fruits of actions is followed immediately by peace.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 12; Paramahamsa Yogananda's translation

quotes.text: He who is free from hatred toward all creatures, is friendly and kind to all, is devoid of the consciousness of "I-ness" and possessiveness; is evenminded in suffering and joy, forgiving, ever contented; a regular yoga practitioner, constantly trying by yoga to know the Self and to unite with Spirit, possessed of firm determination, with mind and discrimination surrendered to Me - he is My devotee, dear to Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 13-14; Paramahamsa Yogananda's translation

quotes.text: A person who does not disturb the world and who cannot be disturbed by the world, who is free from exultation, jealousy, apprehension, and worry - he too is dear to Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 15; Paramahamsa Yogananda's translation

quotes.text: He who is free from worldly expectations, who is pure in body and mind, who is ever ready to work, who remains unconcerned with and unafflicted by circumstances, who has forsaken all ego initiated desireful undertakings - he is My devotee, dear to Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 16; Paramahamsa Yogananda's translation

quotes.text: He who feels neither rejoicing not loathing toward the glad nor the sad (aspects of phenomenal life), who is free from grief and cravings, who has banished the relative consciousness of good and evil, and who is intently devout - he is dear to Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 17; Paramahamsa Yogananda translation

quotes.text: He who is tranquil before friend and foe alike, and in encountering adoration and insult, and during the experiences of warmth and chill and of pleasure and suffering; who has relinquished attachment, regarding blame and praise in the same light; who is quiet and easily contented, not attached to domesticity, and of calm disposition and devotional - that person is dear to Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 18-19; Paramahamsa Yogananda translation

quotes.text: But those who adoringly pursue this undying religion (dharma) as heretofore declared, saturated with devotion, supremely engrossed in Me - such devotees are extremely dear to Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 12, verse 20; Paramahamsa Yogananda translation

quotes.text: This body, O Kaunteya, is called the Field; he who knows it is called knower of the Field by those who know. And understand Me to be, O Bharata, the knower of the Field in all the Fields; and the knowledge of the Field and the knower of the Field, I hold, is true knowledge.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 13, verses 1–2; Mahatma Gandhi translation

quotes.text: O Arjuna! The Supreme Self, having no beginning, (no ending,) and no attributes, even though it dwells in a body (as a realized master), neither acts nor is touched by any action.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 13, verse 31; Swami Kriyananda edition

quotes.text: Those who live in Sattva go upwards; those in rajas remain where they are. But those immersed in tamas sink downwards. The wise see clearly that all action is the work of the gunas. Knowing that which is above the gunas, they enter into union with me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 14, verses 18–19; Eknath Easwaran translation

quotes.text: There is a fig tree In ancient story, The giant Aswattha, The everlasting, Rooted in heaven, Its branches earthward: Each of its leaves Is a song of the Vedas, And he who knows it Knows all the Vedas.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 15, verse 1; Swami Prabhavananda and Christopher Isherwood translation

quotes.text: It is I who remain seated in the heart of all creatures as the inner controller of all; and it is I who am the source of memory, knowledge and the ratiocinative faculty. Again, I am the only object worth knowing through the Vedas; I alone am the origin of Vedānta and the knower of the Vedas too.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 15, verse 15; Gita Press translation (code: 1658)

quotes.text: There are two Beings (Purushas) in the cosmos, the destructible and the indestructible. The creatures are the destructible, the Kutastha is the indestructible. But there exists Another, the Highest Being, designated the "Supreme Spirit"—the Eternal Lord who, permeating the three worlds, upholds them.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 15, verses 16–17; Paramahansa Yogananda translation

quotes.text: Since I am wholly beyond the perishable world of matter or Ksetra, and am superior even to the imperishable soul, Jivatma, hence I am known as the Purushottama, the Supreme Self, in the world as well as in the Vedas.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 15, verse 18; Gita Press translation

quotes.text: These cruel and wretched haters, the vilest of men, I continually cast into demoniac wombs in mortal worlds. Fallen into demoniac wombs, deluded birth after birth, O son of Kunti, they, instead of attaining to Me, tread the lowest path.
Hell has three gates – lust, anger, and greed; for your own sake, Arjuna, give up these three.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 16, verse 21; Purushottama Lal translation

quotes.text: Pure men worship the Shining Ones; the passionate the gnomes and giants; the others, the dark folk, worship ghosts and troops of nature-spirits.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 17, verse 4; Annie Besant translation

quotes.text: What's the nature of asceticism, i want to know how's renunciation different
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 18, verse 1; Mani Rao translation

quotes.text: Asceticism is giving up selfish activities as poets know & the wise declare renunciation is giving up fruits of action
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verse 2; Mani Rao translation

quotes.text: Acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; worship, charity, and also austerity, are the purifiers of even the 'wise'. But even these actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the fruits, O Partha; this is my certain and best belief.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verses 5–6; Swami Chinmayananda commentary

quotes.text: Better is one's own duty though performed faultily than another's duty well-performed. Performing the duty prescribed by (one's own) nature, one incurreth no sin. One must not abandon, O son of Kunti, one's natural duty though tainted with evil, for all actions are enveloped by evil like fire by smoke.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verses 47–48; Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation

quotes.text: If, having recourse to self-conceit, thou thinkest--I will not fight,--that resolution of thine would be vain, (for) Nature will constrain thee. That which, from delusion, thou dost not wish to do, thou wilt do involuntarily, bound by thy own duty springing from (thy own) nature.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verses 59–60; Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation

quotes.text: If you become conscious of Me, you will pass over all the obstacles of conditional life by My grace. If, however, you do not work in such consciousness but act through false ego, not hearing Me, you will be lost. If you do not act according to My direction and do not fight, then you will be falsely directed. By your nature, you will have to be engaged in warfare. Under illusion you are now declining to act according to My direction. But, compelled by your own nature, you will act all the same, O son of Kuntī.
quotes.cite: Verses 59 & 60, Swami Prabhupada translation, 1972

quotes.text: The Supreme Lord is situated in everyone's heart, O Arjuna, and is directing the wanderings of all living entities, who are seated as on a machine, made of the material energy.
quotes.cite: Verse 61, Swami Prabhupada translation, 1972

quotes.text: O Arjuna, God resides in the hearts of all beings, directing their wanderings by the magical power of Māyā, on which they are seated as if it were a machine.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verse 61; The Times of India translation

quotes.text: In him alone seek refuge with all thy being, Bharata; by his grace shalt thou win to peace supreme, the eternal resting place.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verse 62; W. Douglas P. Hill translation

quotes.text: Thus I have explained to you the most confidential of all knowledge. Deliberate on this fully, and then do what you wish to do.
quotes.cite: Chapter 18, verse 63; trans. A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda

quotes.text: All duty abandoning, to me, the sole refuge, come; i will liberate you from every sin, do not grieve.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verse 66; Ramesh Menon translation

quotes.text: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reaction. Do not fear.
quotes.cite: Verse 66, Swami Prabhupada translation, 1972

quotes.text: Never share these truths with one who is without self-control or devotion, nor with one who won't share with others in a spirit of service, nor give them to one who is indifferent to them, or who finds fault with Me.
quotes.cite: Krishna; Chapter 18, verse 67; Swami Kriyananda edition

quotes.text: And one who listens with faith and without envy becomes free from sinful reaction and attains to the planets where the pious dwell.
quotes.cite: Sanjaya; Chapter 18, verse 71; Geoffrey Parrinder translation

quotes.text: Krishna, my delusion is destroyed, And by your grace I have regained memory; I stand here, my doubt dispelled, ready to act on your words.
quotes.cite: Arjuna; Chapter 18, verse 73; Barbara Stoler Miller translation

quotes.text: I heard by grace of Vyasa of Krishna’s highest mystery, Yoga from the Lord of Yoga explaining personally.
quotes.cite: Sanjaya; Chapter 18, verse 75; Geoffrey Parrinder translation

quotes.text: Where Krishna is the Master of combinations, where Partha is the wielder of the bow, there, I am convinced, would be glory, victory, growth and firm morality.
quotes.cite: Sanjaya; Chapter 18, verse 78 (the last verse in the Bhagavad Gita); Jogindranath Mukharji translation

quotes.text: Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, the master of all mystics, and wherever there is Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will also certainly be opulence, victory, extraordinary power, and morality.
quotes.cite: Verse 78, Swami Prabhupada translation, 1972
